page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor featuring 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high resource density of 16.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Additionally, the instance includes 3780 GB of bundled local storage and is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core and multi-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2110.0 and a multi-core score of 16603.0. The processor excels in integer and cryptographic operations, supported by advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX. However, memory performance presents a clear tradeoff; while cached small-block read bandwidth is high at 2465.6 GB/sec, the PassMark memory score is relatively weak at 1572.37. Large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidths are measured at 181.85 GB/sec and 74.71 GB/sec, respectively.

This server is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive enterprise workloads that require a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio without the added cost of dedicated GPUs. It is well-suited for large-scale database operations, static web serving, and memory-bound data processing. While it handles small to medium LLM inference tasks adequately, it is poorly suited for large-scale LLM text generation, where it achieves only 2.45 tokens/sec on a 70B model.
